en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Polytheists were departing from before the disappearance of the sun, so Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> opposed them, and he<sup>saww</sup> departed after the setting of the sun’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘When the sun sets, so depart along with the people, and upon you should be the tranquillity and the dignity. And, depart with the seeking of the Forgiveness, for Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [2:199] Then hasten on from where the people hasten on and seek the Forgiveness of Allah; surely Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.

So when you end up to the red dune upon the right of the road, so say, ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Have Mercy upon my pausing, and Increase in my knowledge, and Safeguard my Religion for me, and Accept my rituals’. Beware of the excitement, which the people are doing, for Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘O you people! The Hajj is not with the excitement of the cavalry, nor the racing of the camels. But, fear Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and walk with a beautiful walking, not trampling upon the weak, nor trampling a Muslim, and be considerate and moderate in the walking, for Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> would restrain his<sup>saww</sup> she-camel until its head would touch its front legs, and he<sup>saww</sup> was saying: ‘O you people! It is upon you with the calmness. Thus, you should follow the Sunnah of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>’.

Muawiya (the narrator) said, ‘And I hear Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Emancipate me<sup>asws</sup> from the Fire!’, and he<sup>asws</sup> repeated it until he<sup>asws</sup> departed. So I<sup>asws</sup> said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Are you<sup>asws</sup> not departing, for the people have already departed?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> fear the congestion, and I<sup>asws</sup> fear that I<sup>asws</sup> might participate in impeding (hindering) a person’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn Isma‘il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the pagans would depart ‘Arafat before sunset. The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, opposed them. He departed after sunset.

He (the narrator) has said that abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘When it is sunset, then depart ‘Arafat along with the people in a calm and dignified manner. Ask forgiveness from Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, who has said, “Then depart ‘Arafat as people do and ask forgiveness from Allah; Allah is forgiving and merciful.” [2:198]

When you reach al-Kathib al-Ahmar on the right side of the road say, “O Allah, grant me kindness for my staying in ‘Arafat, increase my knowledge, protect my religion and accept my acts of al-Hajj.” Beware of al-Wajif (moving in a rough and rushing manner) as people do. The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, had said, “O people, al-Hajj is not horse or camel racing. Be God-fearing and walk in a beautiful manner. You must not overrun the weak ones or Muslims. Walk considerately and moderately.” The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, halted his camel until the camel’s head reached the front part of the leg and the Messenger of Allah said, “O people, you must remain calm.” The tradition of the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, must be followed.’

Mu‘awiyah has said, ‘I heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, say, “O Allah, set me free from hellfire.” He (the Imam) repeated it until he departed ‘Arafat. I asked, “Are you not leaving? People have left.” He (the Imam) replied, “I am afraid of congestion and I do not want to cause trouble to a human being.’””
